authorities.proposition: The regional courts of appeals have jurisdiction over final decisions of the United States district courts, subject to statutory exceptions.
Unless another part of section 2107 applies, a civil notice of appeal must be filed within 30 days after entry of the judgment, order, or decree.

authorities.citation: Fed. R. Civ. P. 54(b) (effective Dec. 1, 2025)
authorities.proposition: In a multiple-claim or multiple-party action, entry of final judgment as to fewer than all claims or parties requires an express determination that there is no just reason for delay; otherwise the partial decision remains nonfinal and revisable.

authorities.citation: Fed. R. Civ. P. 58(a), (c) (effective Dec. 1, 2025)
authorities.proposition: A judgment ordinarily must be set out in a separate document, and when a separate document is required entry occurs upon docket entry and the earlier of the separate document or 150 days.

authorities.citation: Fed. R. App. P. 3(a), (c) (Fourth Circuit rulebook Mar. 23, 2026)
authorities.proposition: An appeal as of right is taken by timely filing a notice with the district clerk; the notice identifies the appellant, the appealed judgment or order, and the court of appeals.

authorities.citation: Fed. R. App. P. 4(a)(1)(A) (Fourth Circuit rulebook Mar. 23, 2026)
authorities.proposition: In an ordinary private-party civil case, the notice of appeal must be filed with the district clerk within 30 days after entry of the judgment or order appealed from.

authorities.citation: 4th Cir. Loc. R. 3(b) (Mar. 23, 2026)
authorities.proposition: Counsel filing a direct or cross-appeal must file the court's docketing statement within 14 days after docketing, serve it, and attach any transcript order.

authorities.citation: Fed. R. App. P. 10(a), (b) and 4th Cir. Loc. R. 10 (Mar. 23, 2026)
authorities.proposition: The appellate record consists of the district papers and exhibits, any transcript, and a certified docket; within 14 days after notice the appellant orders necessary transcript or certifies that none will be ordered.

authorities.citation: Fed. R. App. P. 12(a) (Fourth Circuit rulebook Mar. 23, 2026)
authorities.proposition: After receiving the notice of appeal and district docket entries, the circuit clerk dockets the appeal under the district-court title and identifies the appellant.

authorities.citation: Fourth Circuit, Appearance, Disclosure & Docketing Statements (March 2026 page, checked Aug. 11, 2026)
authorities.proposition: Counsel appearance, applicable corporate disclosure, and the appellant's docketing statement are ordinarily filed within 14 days after appellate docketing; the docketing statement includes the transcript order.

authorities.citation: Fed. R. App. P. 26(a), (c) (Fourth Circuit rulebook Mar. 23, 2026)
authorities.proposition: For a period stated in days, exclude the trigger day, count intermediate weekends and legal holidays, and extend a weekend or legal-holiday last day; three additional service days do not apply to electronic service.

authorities.citation: Fed. R. App. P. 30(a) and 4th Cir. Loc. R. 30 (Mar. 23, 2026)
authorities.proposition: The appendix includes relevant docket entries, pertinent pleadings and rulings, the judgment or order under review, and other record portions to which the parties direct the court.

authorities.citation: Fourth Circuit Appendix Pagination & Brief Citation Guide (June 24, 2025)
authorities.proposition: A joint appendix uses continuous Bates pagination, and briefs cite appendix pages using a recognized JA-number format without inserted suffix pages.

authorities.citation: Fed. R. App. P. 31(a) and 4th Cir. Loc. R. 31 (Mar. 23, 2026)
authorities.proposition: Absent a different order, ordinary civil briefing allows 40 days for the opening brief, 30 days after service for the response, and 21 days after service for a reply, subject to the pre-argument limit.

authorities.citation: Fed. R. App. P. 34(a)(2) and 4th Cir. Loc. R. 34(a) (Mar. 23, 2026)
authorities.proposition: A unanimous three-judge panel may decide without oral argument when an issue is authoritatively decided or the briefs and record adequately present it and argument would not significantly aid decision.

authorities.citation: Fed. R. App. P. 36(a), (b) (Fourth Circuit rulebook Mar. 23, 2026)
authorities.proposition: Appellate judgment is entered when noted on the docket, and the clerk serves the opinion or judgment and notice of the entry date that day.

authorities.citation: Fed. R. App. P. 40(d)(1) (Fourth Circuit rulebook Mar. 23, 2026)
authorities.proposition: Unless an order changes the time, a rehearing petition is due 14 days after judgment, or 45 days in specified civil cases involving the United States or its officers or agencies.

authorities.citation: Fed. R. App. P. 41(a)–(c) (Fourth Circuit rulebook Mar. 23, 2026)
authorities.proposition: The mandate contains the certified judgment, any opinion, and costs direction; absent an order it issues seven days after rehearing time expires or seven days after disposition of a timely rehearing petition or stay motion, whichever is later, and is effective when issued.

authorities.citation: Fourth Circuit Hours & Holidays, 2026 calendar (checked Aug. 11, 2026)
authorities.proposition: The court publishes its 2026 federal holidays and additional clerk-office closure dates for calendar and accessibility checks.

authorities.citation: Fourth Circuit, New Appeals & Petitions — Civil Appeals (March 2026 page, checked Aug. 11, 2026)
authorities.proposition: The timely filing of a civil notice of appeal is mandatory and jurisdictional because the civil appeal period is set by 28 U.S.C. § 2107.

authorities.citation: Kinsale Insurance Co. v. JDBC Holdings, Inc., 31 F.4th 870, 873–76 (4th Cir. 2022)
authorities.proposition: Rule 54(b) certification requires an ultimate disposition of an individual claim and a case-specific no-just-reason determination; the inquiry is tilted against fragmentation, applies the Braswell considerations, and should be supported by stated findings.

authorities.citation: McPherson v. Patton, No. 23-1938, slip op. at 4–7 (4th Cir. Oct. 15, 2024) (unpublished)
authorities.proposition: In a nonprecedential disposition, a grant of a Rule 54(b) motion plus a partial judgment did not become final where the court omitted the express no-just-reason determination; the appeal was dismissed and remanded.
